==English== {{wp}} ===Pronunciation=== * {{IPA|en|/lɒk/|a=RP}} * {{enPR|lŏk|a=GA}}, {{IPA|en|/lɑk/}} * {{audio|en|en-us-lock.ogg|a=US}} * {{rhymes|en|ɒk|s=1}} * {{hmp|en|Locke|;|loch|lough|a2=Anglicised}} * {{hmp|en|lakh|;|lark|;|lawk|a=GA,father-bother}} ===Etymology 1=== [[File:Padlock.jpg|thumb|upright|A '''lock''' requiring a key ({{senseno|en|Q228039}})]] [[File:RHK Lock Wanne 2.jpg|thumb|upright|A '''lock''' ({{senseno|en|Q105731}})]] {{etymon|en|id=mechanism|:inh|enm:lok|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|lok}}, from {{inh|en|ang|loc}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*lok}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*luką}} from {{der|en|ine-pro|*lewg-||to bend; turn}}. Cognate with {{cog|cim|loch}}, {{m|cim|lòch|t=hole}}, {{cog|nl|lok|t=hole}}, {{cog|de|Loch|t=hole}}, {{cog|nds-de|Lock|t=hole}}, {{cog|lb|Lach|t=hole}}, {{cog|wym|łöch|t=hole}}, {{cog|yi|לאָך|t=hole}}, {{cog|da|låg|t=lid, cover}}, {{cog|nb|lokk|t=lid, cover}}, {{cog|nn|lok}}, {{m|nn|lokk|t=lid, cover}}. {{col-top|2|more detail}} The verb is from {{inh|en|enm|locken}}, {{m|enm|lokken}}, {{m|enm|louken}}, from {{inh|en|ang|lūcan}}, {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*lūkan}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*lūkaną}}. Cognate with {{cog|nl|luiken||to close, to shut}}, {{cog|da|-}}, {{cog|nb|lukke||to close, to shut}}, {{cog|fo|lúka||to end, to finish}}, {{cog|is|ljúka||to close, to shut}}, {{cog|nn|lukka||to close, to shut}}. Related to {{m|en|luxe}} via Latin. {{col-bottom}} ====Noun==== {{en-noun}} # {{sid|en|Q228039}} Something used for [[fasten]]ing, which can only be opened with a [[key]] or [[combination]]. #* {{RQ:Stevenson Treasure Island|passage="Give me the key," said my mother; and though the '''lock''' was very stiff, she had turned it and thrown back the lid in a twinkling.}} #* {{RQ:Lincoln Pratt's Patients|pages=304–305|pageref=305|passage=We tiptoed into the house, up the stairs and along the hall to the door of the room where the Professor had been spending so much of his time. 'Twas locked, of course, but the Deacon man got a big bunch of keys out of his pocket and commenced to putter with the '''lock'''.}} # {{lb|en|computing|by extension}} A [[mutex]] or other token restricting access to a [[resource]]. # {{sid|en|Q105731}} A segment of a [[canal]] or other [[navigable]] [[waterway]] enclosed by [[gate]]s, used for raising and lowering [[boat]]s between levels. # {{sid|en|Q1134386}} {{lb|en|gun mechanisms}} The firing mechanism in a gun. #* {{RQ:Dickens Pickwick Papers|passage="I never saw such a gun in my life," replied poor Winkle, looking at the '''lock''', as if that would do any good.}} # Complete [[control]] over a situation. # Something sure to be a [[success]]. #* {{quote-book|en|year=2004|author=w:Avery Corman|title=A perfect divorce|passage=Brian thinks she's a '''lock''' to get a scholarship somewhere.}} # {{lb|en|gambling}} {{syn of|en|Dutch book}}. # {{lb|en|rugby}} A player in the [[scrum]] behind the [[front row]], usually the tallest members of the team. # A fastening together or interlacing; a closing of one thing upon another; a state of being fixed or immovable. #* {{RQ:De Quincey Works|volume=II|page=207|passage=[O]n may of his lecture days I have seen all Albemarle Street closed by a "'''lock'''" of carriages, filled with women of distinction, until the servants of the Institution or their own footmen advanced to the carriage-doors with the intelligence that Mr. Coleridge had been suddenly taken ill.}} # A place impossible to get out of, as by a lock. #* {{RQ:Dryden Aeneis|5|passage=Sergestus, eager with his beak to press / Betwixt the rival galley and the rock, / Shuts up the unwieldy Centaur in the '''lock'''}} # A [[device]] for keeping a [[wheel]] from [[turn]]ing. # A [[grapple]] in [[wrestling]]. #* Cognate with {{cog|gsw|lokha|t=hair}}, {{cog|nl|lok|t=lock of hair, curl}}, {{cog|de|Locke|t=lock of hair, curl}}, {{cog|da|lok|t=lock of hair, curl}}, {{cog|fo|-}}, {{cog|is|lokkur|t=lock of hair, curl}}, {{cog|nb|-}}, {{cog|nn|lokk|t=lock of hair, curl}}, {{cog|sv|lock|t=lock of hair, curl}}. It has been theorised that the word may be related to the {{cog|got|-}} verb {{m|got|*𐌻𐌿𐌺𐌰𐌽|t=to shut}} in its ancient meaning "to curb". ====Noun==== {{en-noun}} # {{sid|en|tuft}} A [[tuft]] or [[length]] of [[hair]], [[wool]]{{,}} etc. #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Merchant of Venice|I|i|page=164|passage={{w|Bassanio|''Baſſ.''}} {{...}}Nor is the wide world ignorant of {{w|Portia (The Merchant of Venice)|her}} worth,
For the foure windes blow in from euery coaſt
Renowned ſutors, and her ſunny '''locks'''
Hang on her temples like a golden fleece,
Which makes her ſeat of ''Belmont'' ''[[Colchis|Cholchos]][[-'| ]]'' [[strond|ſtrond]],
And many ''[[Jason|Iaſons]]'' come in queſt of her.}} #* {{RQ:Emily Bronte Wuthering Heights|XXI|text=If I consent to burn them, will you promise faithfully neither to send nor receive a letter again, nor a book (for I perceive you have sent him books), nor '''locks''' of hair, nor rings, nor playthings?}} # A small quantity of [[straw]] etc. # {{lb|en|Scots law|historical}} A quantity of [[meal]], the [[perquisite]] of a [[mill]]-[[servant]]. =====Derived terms===== {{col4|en |daglock |earlock|devilock |elflock |forelock|locklet|locky |goldilocks,Goldilocks|hairlock |hindlock |lovelock |sidelock|soaplock|taglock|underlock}} =====Translations===== {{trans-top-see|length of hair|highlight}} * Afrikaans: * Arabic: * Aramaic: * Bashkir: * Bulgarian: * Burmese: * Catalan: * Cherokee: * Chinese: * Czech: * Danish: * Dhivehi: * Dutch: * Egyptian: * Esperanto: * Estonian: * Finnish: * French: * Friulian: * Galician: * Georgian: * German: * Greek: * Gujarati: * Hungarian: * Icelandic: * Ido: * Ingrian: * Interlingua: * Irish: * Italian: * Japanese: * Khmer: * Korean: * Latin: * Macedonian: * Malayalam: * Māori: * Marathi: * Mirandese: * Odia: * Ossetian: * Polish: * Portuguese: * Punjabi: * Romanian: * Russian: {{t+|ru|ло́кон|m}}, {{t+|ru|прядь|f}} * Slovak: * Slovene: * Somali: * Sorbian: * Spanish: * Swedish: * Tamil: * Telugu: * Thai: * Tocharian B: * Turkish: * Walloon: * Welsh: {{trans-bottom}} ===Etymology 3=== {{ellipsis of|en|dreadlock}} ====Noun==== {{en-noun}} # A single [[dreadlock]]. ====Verb==== {{en-verb}} # To form a dreadlock. ===Anagrams=== * {{anagrams|en|a=cklo|KLOC|Kloc|colk}} {{cln|en|ergative verbs}} {{topics|en|Canals|Dance|Hair|Locks}}
